scope: Availability defects in unpublished candidate; OrbStack Ubuntu Linux arm64; shared host
fixes: nonfatal background snapshot cleanup with protected restore files and inode-bound startup retry
cached periodic diagnostic status with sample freshness; live health and control unchanged
deadline-aware request admission using durable commit position and clamped application lag

dual.check: same image concurrently serves standalone direct, standalone WAL and three-replica Raft; tenant data stays independent
local standalone/WAL and every Raft replica expose finite diagnostic samples
standalone direct commits and ingest survive SIGKILL; compact and GC remain available
standalone WAL accepted response is durable; SIGKILL recovery publishes once and idempotent retry preserves identity
isolated replica diagnostics remain locally readable without quorum
live isolated leader rejects strong reads and writes; majority serves and confirmed write survives reconnection
Raft majority WAL and leader takeover remain available alongside standalone services
standalone offline CLI works; existing standalone directory refuses Raft bootstrap without losing standalone access
Raft replica refuses standalone service and offline writes when Raft settings are omitted; configured restart works
maintenance diagnostic counters reflect completed real work
36 MiB backup restore resumes after leader SIGKILL and invalidates old read generation
snapshot diagnostic counters reflect completed real work
cold full three-replica runtime backup/restore preserves graph, templates, accepted identities and streaming snapshots; writes resume
protocol 3 serial drain/restart/rejoin preserves data with the same qualified binary

sharded.check: standalone direct/WAL coexist with sharded Raft
catalog, shard replicas and authenticated router expose local diagnostics
add three-replica shard without remapping existing tenant
catalog diagnostics expose the blocked migration phase and retained error
chunked migration survives catalog and destination leader interruption
tenant can return to retired source and commit again
one shard loses quorum while other shard and standalones serve
cancel before cutover resumes source before unavailable target cleanup
replica cannot remove shard role; original configuration recovers
gateway keeps known tenant strong reads and idempotent writes during catalog outage; unknown routes fail closed
drained router diagnostics do not require a reachable catalog
